subject: Acme Health - license granularity & SLA stack negotiation
messages:
From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify VPC licensing granularity + SLA/support tiers

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the product overview last week — the team found Redwood's runtime compelling. Procurement asked me to get a tighter picture of how licensing and support would map to our multi-cluster deployment. A few specific asks: 

- Do you sell per-node licenses (per-server) or per-concurrent-unit? Any hybrid options (e.g., per-node for edge sites, metered for central)?
- How is the platform fee amortized for on-prem (monthly vs annual) and are there starter credits for migration?
- What are the explicit SLAs for the three support tiers (standard / enhanced / enterprise)? We need on-call response windows and a clear SLO for failover across regions.

Attached is our SOW sketch (draft) and a procurement checklist — happy to redline. Can we lock a 30-min slot next week to align?

Sara
Sara Cho
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Health

Attachment: SOW-draft-acme.docx (attachment stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify VPC licensing granularity + SLA/support tiers

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a proposal so procurement has something concrete to review before the call: 

- License granularity: we offer three principal models for private deployments:
  1) Node-based (per GPU-node) — recommended for stable, capacity-planned clusters.
  2) Metered (vCPU/GPU-hour) — recommended for bursty or seasonal workloads.
  3) Hybrid — you can anchor a baseline of node licenses for critical sites and add metered capacity for central burst traffic.

- Platform fee amortization: typically annual invoicing with monthly technical support allocation. If you prefer monthly cash flow we can convert to monthly invoicing at a small premium (1.75% fee). We also have a one-time migration credit that scales by commit (details below).

- Support tiers SLA highlights:
  Standard — 24h business-day response, next-business-day incident triage.
  Enhanced — 4h business-day response, 24/7 paging for Sev 1 during business-critical windows.
  Enterprise — 1h response 24/7, named SRE on-call + quarterly on-site reviews.

I've attached a term sheet with a matrix and two starter scenarios (node-anchored and hybrid). Can you confirm your expected baseline concurrent inference nodes across sites (edge + central) ahead of the meeting? If you don't have precise counts, a best-effort estimate will do.

Proposed 30-min slots: Tue 5 Aug 10am PT or Wed 6 Aug 11am PT.

Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_VPC_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify VPC licensing granularity + SLA/support tiers

Adding a bit of product/ops color from my side — this is Neha (solutions lead, infra deployments). A couple of notes to make the procurement review easier: 

- SLA stack: the "Enterprise" tier includes a 99.95% regional uptime SLO for the serving control plane and a separate 99.9% SLO for customer-managed network connectivity checks. We put the network SLO in a carve-out (customer-owned infra exceptions) but provide runbook-backed diagnostics.

- Migration credit mechanics: for an annual commit >= $750k we can offer a time-boxed migration credit equal to 15% of year-1 platform fee (applied as invoice credit over first 3 months). For a commit >= $1.25M we can move that to 25% applied over first 6 months.

- Security add-ons (SOC2 evidence, KMS integrations) are billable under professional services; we typically include 12 hours of onboarding per cluster in the migration credit calculation.

If you'd like, I can draft a short footnote that procurement can paste into the PO to capture the credit mechanics.

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Lead, Infra Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify VPC licensing granularity + SLA/support tiers

Thanks Neha — that's helpful. Sara, based on your original note and Neha's mechanics, here's a concrete concession package for Acme to review before procurement: 

Option A — Node-anchored (recommended for clinical clusters):
- Baseline: 40 node licenses (on-prem GPU nodes) at $X/node/year.
- Platform fee: annual $240k, amortized monthly on invoice.
- Support: Enhanced (4h response) included in year 1.
- Migration credit: 15% of platform fee (applied as three monthly credits) if you sign the annual commit within 30 days.

Option B — Hybrid (central metered burst + edge anchors):
- Baseline: 20 node licenses + metered pool for central inference.
- Platform fee: annual $180k with enterprise support add-on at $70k/year.
- Migration credit: 20% of platform fee applied over first 4 months for a $1M+ commit.

Operational clarifications:
- We will provide a named technical account manager for onboarding for any Enterprise/Enhanced deal.
- On-call handoff: we propose a 30-day runbook co-validation window; after that on-call escalation transfers to Redwood per the chosen support tier.

Next steps: if these options look directionally correct, can procurement provide preferred PO language and an internal redline window? We'll prepare a clean SOW (attached) and a short PO footnote documenting the migration-credit calculation.

Thanks — I'll hold Tue 5 Aug 10am PT as a tentative slot.

Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_VPC_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf, SOW-draft-acme.docx (attachment stubs)

From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-ops@acmehealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify VPC licensing granularity + SLA/support tiers

Jonas / Neha — thanks, that level of granularity is exactly what procurement needed. A couple quick follow-ups before we escalate to legal: 

1) Can you convert the Option A numbers into a simple two-line PO example (line 1: 40 node licenses, line 2: platform fee) with the 15% migration credit shown as an invoice credit line? Procurement wants to paste it into the PO template.
2) For the Enterprise SLA "1h response 24/7" — please confirm whether that includes phone paging or only in-platform escalation. We need phone paging to be explicit for our critical patient-facing endpoints.

We are targeting internal approval by EOD next Friday. If you can drop the PO example and a one-sentence confirmation on phone paging by EOD Friday 7 Aug, I'll circulate to legal and procurement for redlines.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Sara Cho
Director, Cloud Platform
Acme Health
